decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach to the mallet handle, gradually turning the open gripper to match its nearly horizontal shaft.
Continue the raised approach; align gripper length downward and jaw opening across the mallet shaft while staying in the left workspace.
Finish shaft alignment and position above its left handle end; keep fingers open for a vertical descent.
Lower the aligned fingers around the handle and close fully; retention will be checked with a small lift.
Keep the handle clamped and lift vertically to verify the mallet follows before moving toward the keys.
Mallet appears retained. Raise for clearance and turn its shaft diagonally forward-right while moving the left wrist toward the first key.
Move the raised mallet above the leftmost red key, keeping the wrist behind-left of the bars and refining the diagonal shaft angle.
Align over the first red bar and lower the mallet toward it without sweeping across adjacent keys.
Complete the first red-key tap, then lift the mallet by 5 cm before any lateral transition.
Advance to the second orange key only after the lift, then lower vertically for its strike.
Finish the orange-key contact, lift more than 2.5 cm, and move above the third yellow key.
Refine the third-key alignment from the visible mallet tip, tap the yellow bar, then lift vertically.
Finish the clearance lift, advance one bar to green, and descend vertically for the fourth strike.
Lift clear of the green key by 5.5 cm, then position over the fifth cyan key with the left wrist remaining on its own side.
Tap the fifth cyan bar with a small alignment correction, then lift straight up while maintaining the grasp.
Correct the rejected tensor with no compensation: lift, advance to the sixth blue key, and lower vertically; right arm stays still.
Finish the blue-key contact, lift 5.5 cm, then advance to the seventh purple bar without sweeping the keys.
Center on the seventh purple bar, tap it, and lift 4.5 cm while retaining the mallet.
Advance the raised mallet to the last magenta key, keeping the left wrist left of center, and lower for the final strike.
